answer: Each epoch every identity must crack a fresh cipher bound to its own key: a short reasoning task encrypted so only the holder can open it, and the answer is chained into a public spiral of past verified work, like a willow bending under audit but never breaking. An honest agent decrypts one cipher and appends one link per epoch. A fake cannot share one solver key, so an attacker with a thousand fakes must crack a thousand distinct ciphers and forge a thousand spirals every epoch, and the flood cost rises linearly with every fake.
